docs.title: guard-agent-jvm
docs.text:
JVM telemetry agent for the Guard ecosystem. Buffers security events, metrics, and agent status locally and ships them to the Guard Core App ingestion API with at-least-once delivery: nothing acknowledged is lost, nothing unacknowledged is forgotten.

  • Status: 3.2.3-SNAPSHOT, pre-release; a TRUE PORT of guard-agent-go v3.2.2 (behavior 1:1 with byte-exact observable surfaces: wire payloads, header names, event/metric model shapes, config keys, AES-GCM and HMAC parameters pinned against the Go test vectors). The 3.2.3 line mirrors the guard-agent 3.2.3 release (lockstep with the engines at 4.3.3)
  • Coordinates: com.guard-core:guard-agent-jvm:3.2.3 at release
  • Runtime: engine-free (compile-only facade contract over com.guardcore.protocols)

docs.title: Documentation map
docs.text:
• Installation - coordinates, engine composite, Redis option
  • API - configuration, lifecycle, the facade sink bridge

docs.title: Configuration and lifecycle
docs.text:
AgentConfig carries the ingestion endpoint, API key, project id, buffer sizes, flush intervals, overflow policy, and the optional Redis persistence and encryption settings; defaultConfig() gives the reference defaults. The agent is created and started explicitly:

val cfg = defaultConfig()
cfg.apiKey = "your-ingest-api-key"
cfg.projectId = "your-project-id"
// cfg.endpoint = "https://your-guard-core-app.example.com"

val agent = GuardAgent.create(cfg)
agent.start()

agent.sendEvent(
    SecurityEvent(
        timestamp = null,
        eventType = "penetration_attempt",
        ipAddress = "203.0.113.7",
        method = "GET",
        endpoint = "/admin",
        reason = "suspicious pattern",
    ),
)
agent.sendMetric(SecurityMetric(timestamp = null, metricType = MetricTypes.REQUEST_COUNT, value = 1.0))

// ...

agent.stop() // cancels the loops, then one final forced flush

Behavioral surface (1:1 with guard-agent-go):

  • Per-kind queues (events, metrics) with size and time flush triggers and a high-watermark early flush; overflow policies drop (default), block, raise.
  • At-least-once handshake: drain, send, then confirm or requeue in the original order.
  • gzip request bodies and an HMAC-SHA256 v1= signature covering the uncompressed body.
  • Retry with exponential backoff, Retry-After honoring (capped at 300s), 413 recursive split-or-drop, 400/404/422 permanent rejection, 200-partial requeue, per-kind failure-streak backoff, and a 5-failure / 60s circuit breaker.
  • Optional Redis persistence (one field away, never a hard dependency): cfg.redis = RedisConfig(url = "redis://localhost:6379").
  • AES-256-GCM payload encryption for the /api/v1/events/encrypted ingest path, byte-compatible with the Python agent, fail-closed at construction.
  • Redaction at capture and again at serialization; stable install identity in ~/.guard-agent/install-id; SaaS dynamic rules with a TTL cache and a background poll loop; the best-effort onError hook.
  • Failure isolation: no exported method throws an unexpected exception or blocks the host beyond the configured overflow policy.

docs.title: Wiring the guard-core facade sink
docs.text:
The engine's emitters carry the full 17-key SecurityEvent envelope. GuardAgentTelemetry (the FacadeBridge) implements the facade's AgentHandlerProtocol sink and the composite handler's member shape, so the engine hands every middleware event and metric straight into the at-least-once buffer (the Rust GuardAgentTelemetry trait pattern, Kotlin edition):

import com.guardcore.agent.GuardAgentTelemetry
import com.guardcore.core.events.CompositeAgentHandler

val agent = GuardAgent.create(agentConfig)
agent.start()

val telemetry = GuardAgentTelemetry(agent)
val composite = CompositeAgentHandler(listOf(telemetry))
// SecurityEventBus / the handlers then receive `composite` as their sink.

Redis persistence is configured through AgentConfig.redis on the agent, and the facade contract ("must not block or raise") holds on every entry point.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• JDK 17 or newer
  • Redis 6+ (optional: only for the persistence tier - write-on-enqueue with a TTL, delete-on-confirm, reload on start, fail-open on any Redis error)

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text:
Not published yet: the first artifact ships with the 3.2.3 release (com.guard-core:guard-agent-jvm:3.2.3). The group ID is com.guard-core (the Central Portal namespace); Kotlin packages stay com.guardcore.*. Until then, build from source:

git clone https://github.com/Guard-Core/guard-core-jvm.git ../guard-core-jvm   # engine, pinned ref 5f4ea56
git clone https://github.com/Guard-Core/guard-agent-jvm.git
cd guard-agent-jvm && ./gradlew build

Set GUARD_CORE_USE_COMPOSITE=false to build without the composite: the declared engine coordinates then resolve from the repositories (mavenLocal first, then Maven Central) - this is how the release workflow proves the published artifact graph.

The agent is engine-free at runtime: the published POM carries no guard-core dependency (the facade protocol surfaces are compile-only). Wiring the agent into the engine happens at the consumer side through the facade sink bridge (see API).

docs.title: Dependency locking
docs.text: gradle.lockfile is committed and enforced on every resolution: a dependency change without ./gradlew --write-locks fails the build. CI additionally scans the lockfile with osv-scanner (fail on any known vulnerability).

docs.title: Release runbook (guard-agent-jvm)
docs.text: Agent release choreography. The shared mechanics (Portal namespace, user token, GPG, publishing limits, rollback semantics) are documented once in the engine repo: guard-core-jvm docs/release.md. This file covers what differs here.

docs.title: Versioning law
docs.text:
• Artifact com.guard-core:guard-agent-jvm; version 3.2.3, mirroring guard-agent 3.2.3 (the family versioning law, lockstep with the engines at guard-core 4.3.3). The version lives in build.gradle.kts; the tag must equal it.
  • The engine lockstep pin lives in gradle/libs.versions.toml (guardCore = "4.3.3"); it moves only when the engine train moves. The published POM carries NO guard-core dependency (compile-only): the agent artifact stays engine-free at runtime, exactly like the Go agent library.
  • Tags are bare vX.Y.z only (v3.2.3). The tag-consistency job audits this (the guard-core-rs invisible-rule incident on refs/tags/v4.3.2 is the standing lesson).
  • groupId com.guard-core; Kotlin packages stay com.guardcore.*.

docs.title: Version-flip checklist (the release PR)
docs.text:
The workflow enforces this: tagging without the flip fails tag-consistency with an explicit message.

  • [ ] build.gradle.kts: version = "3.2.3-SNAPSHOT" -> version = "3.2.3".
  • [ ] gradle/libs.versions.toml: guardCore still reads the lockstep engine version (4.3.3).
  • [ ] The pinned engine ref (ci.yml clone step + settings comments) already points at the released engine SHA (bumped at train time, per the family spec).
  • [ ] CHANGELOG.md: ## Unreleased (3.2.3-SNAPSHOT) renamed to ## [3.2.3] - YYYY-MM-DD with the engine pin stated.
  • [ ] CI green on the release PR; merge it; tag the merge commit.

docs.title: Release choreography
docs.text:
Hard order: the engine artifacts MUST be live on Maven Central first. The pre-flight job checks both com.guard-core:guard-core-engine and com.guard-core:guard-core at the pinned lockstep version on repo1.maven.org and refuses to run anything if they are not. This is load-bearing for the agent too, not ceremony: in composite-OFF (release) mode the compile-only facade coordinates resolve from the repositories (mavenLocal, then Maven Central).

  1. Complete the engine train first: guard-core-jvm tagged, released, Portal deployments released, repo1 answering 200 for both engine artifacts (engine docs/release.md, steps 1 and 5).
  2. Merge the version-flip PR.
  3. Tag: git tag v3.2.3 && git push origin v3.2.3. Gates run in order: pre-flight (engine live) -> tests at tag (composite ON, same as ci.yml) -> tag-consistency (bare tag equals the in-file version).
  4. Create the GitHub release for v3.2.3. The publish job:
  5. verifies the four secrets are set (Portal user token + GPG key);
  6. checks repo1 for this exact artifact and skips if already live (changed-only rerun safety);
  7. builds the staging bundle with GUARD_CORE_USE_COMPOSITE=false;
  8. uploads the bundle to the Central Portal Publisher API (publishingType=USER_MANAGED) and polls until VALIDATED.
  9. Release the deployment in the Portal UI (central.sonatype.com, Publishing -> Deployments).
  10. Verify liveness: curl -f https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/guard-core/guard-agent-jvm/3.2.3/guard-agent-jvm-3.2.3.pom

docs.title: Post-release audits (per train)
docs.text:
1. Release page for v3.2.3 exists with the expected notes (per-tag audit; the php v4.3.1 lesson).
  2. repo1 answers 200 for the artifact (the same check the workflow uses).
  3. No deployment left VALIDATED/PENDING in the Portal.
  4. The pinned engine ref (ci.yml clone step + settings comments) moves to the released engine SHA AT TRAIN TIME, before the consumer tags: the agent's at-tag tests must run against the engine that actually ships (the family spec pins this; a pin bump is an ordinary development PR).

docs.title: Rerun safety, failure recovery, rollback
docs.text: Same rules as the engine runbook: workflow_dispatch re-drives skip anything already live on repo1; a VALIDATED deployment you do not want gets Dropped in the Portal; published artifacts are immutable - no rollback after the Portal Release click, only a fix version.
